title: Chevalley line stabilizers with cancellation of their character
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $G$ an affine group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-pc-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $H\subseteq G$ a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. A finite-dimensional rational representation means a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] with a group-scheme homomorphism $G\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$; after a choice of basis, $\mathrm{GL}(V)=\mathrm{GL}_{\dim V,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group]. Put $V_A=V\otimes_k A$ for a commutative $k$-algebra $A$. A character of $H$ is a group-scheme homomorphism $\chi:H\to\mathbf G_m$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. Say that $\chi$ occurs if there are such a representation $V$ and a nonzero subspace $U\subseteq V$ with $h u=\chi_A(h)u$ for every $A$, $h\in H(A)$ and $u\in U_A$. Assume that whenever $\chi$ occurs, $\chi^{-m}$ occurs for some integer $m>0$, where $\chi^{-m}_A(h)=\chi_A(h)^{-m}$. Then there are a finite-dimensional rational representation $V$ of $G$ and a one-dimensional subspace $L\subseteq V$ such that $H$ fixes $L$ pointwise and is its scheme-theoretic stabilizer. Explicitly, for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$,
$$H(A)=\{g\in G(A):gL_A=L_A\},\qquad h|_{L_A}=\mathrm{id}_{L_A}\quad(h\in H(A)).$$ Here $\mathrm{GL}(V)(A)$ means the $A$-linear automorphisms of $V\otimes_k A$; if $V=0$, this is the trivial group scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$.

source.place: Theorem 4.27 and Corollary 4.29, printed pp.94--95; Remark 4.30, p.96, specifies the stabilizer on all algebras. The inverse character in Corollary 4.29 is written multiplicatively here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-chevalley-scheme-line-stabilizer] to obtain $(E,D)$ with stabilizer $H$ on every algebra. Choose $0\ne e\in D$. Restriction of the representation to $H$ acts on $D_A=Ae$ by a unit $\chi_A(h)$. This is a character $H\to\mathbf G_m$ [def-sc-gm-ga]: in a basis beginning with $e$, its coordinate is the $(1,1)$ matrix coefficient restricted to $H$, its inverse is the same coefficient evaluated at $h^{-1}$, and matrix multiplication on $D$ gives multiplicativity. Thus $\chi$ occurs. The hypothesis supplies $m>0$, a rational representation $F$, and a nonzero scalar-action subspace $U\subseteq F$ of character $\chi^{-m}$. Choose $0\ne f\in U$ and put $B=kf$. Then $H$ acts on $B_A$ by $\chi_A^{-m}$.

source.place: Corollary 4.29, printed p.95, using Theorem 4.27 and Proposition 4.6; the scalar-action subspace is reduced to a line and the tensor-stabilizer calculation is written explicitly.

proof.text: Set $V=E^{\otimes m}\otimes_k F$ and $L=k(e^{\otimes m}\otimes f)$. Tensor bases show that $V$ is finite-dimensional and $L$ is one-dimensional. Give $V$ the diagonal action $\rho_E(g)^{\otimes m}\otimes\rho_F(g)$. This is rational: in tensor bases its matrix entries are products of the entries of the original representation matrices; replacing $g$ by $g^{-1}$ supplies its inverse, and multiplication is respected on pure tensors. For every $A$ and $h\in H(A)$, the generator of $L_A$ is multiplied by $\chi_A(h)^m\chi_A(h)^{-m}=1$. Thus $H(A)$ fixes $L_A$ pointwise and is contained in its stabilizer.

source.place: Corollary 4.29, printed p.95, using Theorem 4.27 and Proposition 4.6; the scalar-action subspace is reduced to a line and the tensor-stabilizer calculation is written explicitly.

proof.text: Conversely let $A$ be any nonzero commutative $k$-algebra and $g\in G(A)$ stabilize $L_A$. Write $x=\rho_E(g)e$ and $y=\rho_F(g)f$. There is a unit $c\in A^\times$ with $x^{\otimes m}\otimes y=c e^{\otimes m}\otimes f$, since restriction to $L_A$ is an automorphism of a free rank-one module. Extend $e,f$ to bases. Their coordinate functionals, composed with the inverse representation matrices, give $A$-linear functionals $\lambda,\mu$ with $\lambda(x)=\mu(y)=1$. Apply $\mathrm{id}\otimes\lambda^{\otimes(m-1)}\otimes\mu$ to the displayed tensor equality. It gives $x=a e$, where $a=c\lambda(e)^{m-1}\mu(f)$. Applying $\lambda$ yields $1=a\lambda(e)$, so $a$ is a unit. Therefore $gD_A=D_A$ and the equality in [lem-sfb-chevalley-scheme-line-stabilizer] gives $g\in H(A)$. For the zero algebra all group-of-points sets are singletons, so the equality holds there too. All actions and subspaces are base extensions of the specified $k$-objects; hence these equalities hold naturally on every algebra and give exactly the claimed scheme-theoretic stabilizer.
